defaults.permitted_development: Across Herefordshire, domestic solar panels are usually easiest on the planning permission route when they sit close to the roof or wall, stay visually secondary to the building and avoid awkward heritage or frontage impacts. Open plots and wider roof visibility can make garden arrays, outbuilding roofs and ancillary equipment more important to the planning story.

rules.height_rules: Solar panels are usually lowest risk when the array and mounting system do not add noticeable height or make the building visually bulkier.
rules.depth_rules: Projection from the roof or wall matters because deeper frames and freestanding equipment can quickly move the installation away from a routine domestic appearance.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary-facing arrays, visible side elevations and garden-based equipment usually deserve a closer amenity and visual check across Herefordshire.
rules.roof_rules: The easiest solar schemes usually follow the roof plane cleanly and avoid sensitive, highly visible or heritage-affected roof slopes.
rules.materials_rules: Panels, inverters and associated equipment should be designed as one tidy appearance-led package rather than as separate add-ons scattered around the building.

rules.permitted_development: In Herefordshire, solar panels are usually easiest to keep off the formal planning permission route when they sit close to the roof or wall, stay visually secondary to the building and avoid awkward heritage or frontage impacts. The route usually gets harder where the most efficient panel layout is also the most visually exposed roof slope or frontage.

rules.height_rules: In Herefordshire, the planning route usually gets harder where solar panels rely on raised frames, extra height, freestanding arrays or associated equipment that makes the installation feel noticeably bulkier.
rules.depth_rules: Projection from the roof or wall matters in Herefordshire because deeper frames and freestanding arrays are usually more visually sensitive than a tight roof-mounted scheme.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary-facing arrays, side elevations and garden equipment often deserve the earliest visual and neighbour check in Herefordshire.
rules.roof_rules: Roof-mounted panels in Herefordshire are usually easiest where they follow the roof slope cleanly and avoid highly visible or heritage-sensitive roof surfaces.
rules.materials_rules: A tidy appearance and finish for panels and ancillary kit usually helps a solar scheme in Herefordshire far more than visibly cluttered cabling, boxes or mismatched equipment.

restrictions.conservation_area: Solar panels in conservation areas within Herefordshire often need a closer design review where they affect visible roof slopes, walls or the wider character of the area.
restrictions.listed_building: Solar works to listed buildings or buildings in their curtilage in Herefordshire usually need a more careful planning and heritage consent check.
